relevance_reason: Reports 14 new patients with biallelic PNPLA8 variants spanning the PNPLA8-related neurological spectrum, including mitochondrial respiration defects in patient fibroblasts, genotype-phenotype correlations, and iPSC cerebral organoid models. This adds clinical, molecular and functional evidence about PNPLA8-related disease, the gene behind this entry.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) reported 14 individuals (6 male, 8 female) from 12 unrelated families, many consanguineous and from countries including Japan, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Turkey, Lebanon, Egypt and Iran, who had neurological disease and biallelic PNPLA8 variants. Age at last assessment ranged from 3 days to 33 years. Frequent features were central hypotonia (13/13), dystonia (8/12), seizures (10/14) and cerebellar atrophy (12/12).
quotes: We identified 14 individuals (six male and eight female individuals) showing neurological manifestations from 12 unrelated families with biallelic variants in PNPLA8 (Fig. 1A). The age of the patients at the last assessment ranged from 3 days to 33 years of age (Table 1).
Highly frequent clinical features of our patients were central hypotonia (100%, 13/13), dystonia (67%, 8/12), seizure (71%, 10/14) and cerebellar atrophy (100%, 12/12).
findings.population: Japan; Saudi Arabia; Iraq; Afghanistan; Pakistan; Turkey; Lebanon; Egypt; Iran

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) described 8 patients (Families 1-8) at the severe end of the spectrum. They had congenital microcephaly (5/7), global developmental delay with no milestones attained (7/7), peripheral spasticity (7/8) and seizure onset within 7 months of age (8/8). Neuroimaging showed a simplified gyral pattern (6/6), pontocerebellar hypoplasia (7/7) and severe progressive cerebral cortical atrophy (5/5).
quotes: eight patients (Families 1–8; Fig. 1B–D) were characterized further by several common features, such as congenital microcephaly (71%, 5/7), global developmental delay attaining no milestones (100%, 7/7), peripheral spasticity (88%, 7/8) and early-onset seizure within 7 months of age (100%, 8/8).

Neuroimaging revealed that these patients showed a simplified gyral pattern (100%, 6/6), pontocerebellar hypoplasia (100%, 7/7) and severe progressive atrophy of the cerebral cortex (100%, 5/5; Fig. 1E–R).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) described 4 patients (Families 11-12) with a relatively mild phenotype. All learned to walk (4/4) and then lost milestones (4/4); 3 of 4 had ataxia and 3 of 4 had mild or no intellectual disability, and seizures were unique or absent. Brain MRI showed little or no cerebral cortical volume loss but progressive cerebellar atrophy. Two further patients (Families 9 and 10) were of intermediate severity.
quotes: four patients (Families 11–12) were characterized by relatively mild features: attaining the milestone of walking (100%, 4/4), ataxia (75%, 3/4), regression of milestones (100%, 4/4), mild or no intellectual disability (75%, 3/4) and unique or absent seizures (100%, 4/4).

Brain MRI showed little or no cerebral cortical volume loss but progressive cerebellar atrophy, consistent with the pronounced movement disorder observed in patients (100%, 3/3; Fig. 1V–Y and Supplementary Videos 1 and 2).

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found 14 PNPLA8 variants, 12 of them novel, by exome or genome sequencing with Sanger segregation analysis. They comprised 4 nonsense, 5 frameshift, 3 intronic variants near exon-intron boundaries and 2 missense variants. Every variant had a frequency below 0.001% in population databases (dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, jMorp and gnomAD), and 12 of the 14 individuals carried combinations of nonsense, frameshift and splice-site variants, suggesting loss of function.
quotes: We identified 14 variants, of which 12 were novel. Of the 14 variants, four were nonsense, five were frameshift, three were intronic variants near an exon–intron boundary, and two were missense variants.
Collectively, 12 of 14 individuals carried the combination of nonsense, frameshift and splice-site variants, which suggests LoF in PNPLA8.

findings.statement: In Patient 1 (Family 1), Nakamura et al. (2024) found the PNPLA8 intronic variant c.1625+3_1625+6del. In patient lymphoblastoid cells it caused skipping of exons 6-8 through aberrant splicing, and the patient's fibroblasts showed a significant reduction of the 77-kDa PNPLA8 protein, indicating a null effect.
quotes: c.1625+3_1625+6del identified in the patient from Family 1 (Patient 1) was assessed using patient blood-derived lymphoblastoid cell lines. Sequencing of each separated transcript by TA cloning revealed that c.1625+3_1625+6del resulted in the skipping of exons 6–8 owing to aberrant splicing
Immunoblotting analysis for the skin fibroblasts from Patient 1 showed a significant reduction in 77-kDa PNPLA8 expression, indicating a null effect of his genetic variants

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) found the PNPLA8 splice-acceptor variants c.2075-2A>G in Patient 2 and c.1684-2A>G in Patient 5. No patient cells were available, but SpliceAI predicted loss of the splice acceptor site, with delta scores of 0.97 and 0.93, respectively.
quotes: Owing to the lack of patient-derived cells, we could not assess experimentally the splicing impact of c.2075-2A>G in Patient 2 and c.1684-2A>G in Patient 5. However, in silico analysis with SpliceAI predicted that c.2075-2A>G and c.1684-2A>G result in the loss of a splice acceptor site with a Δ score of 0.97 and 0.93, respectively

findings.statement: In Patient 6, who had a severe phenotype, Nakamura et al. (2024) found the PNPLA8 frameshift variant p.Glu296Lysfs*6. Like Patient 1's variant, it resulted in a null effect on PNPLA8 protein in skin fibroblasts.
quotes: We found that the LoF variant identified in the severe case (Patient 6: p.Glu296Lysfs*6) resulted in a null effect, similar to Patient 1.

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) combined their patients with 11 previously reported individuals from 8 families and found that biallelic loss-of-function variants affecting 3 or 4 PNPLA8 protein isoforms were associated with the severe phenotype. Patients with a relatively mild neurodegenerative phenotype with late-onset movement disorders all carried biallelic C-terminal frameshift variants (p.Thr757Glnfs*10 or p.Leu759Alafs*4). Intermediate cases carried a loss-of-function variant, missense variants or the recurrent p.Leu759Alafs*4.
quotes: Regarding their genotypes, biallelic LoF variants affecting three or four PNPLA8 protein isoforms were associated specifically with this group (Fig. 2).

Four patients (Families 11–12) and two previously reported adults shared a relatively mild neurodegenerative phenotype characterized by late-onset movement disorders (Table 1 and Supplementary Table 1). All the patients in this group harboured biallelic C-terminal frameshift variants (p.Thr757Glnfs*10 or p.Leu759Alafs*4) (Fig. 2).
These four patients carried the combination of either a LoF variant, missense variants or a recurrent frameshift variant (p.Leu759Alafs*4) located at the C-terminus (Fig. 2).

findings.statement: In skin fibroblasts, Nakamura et al. (2024) found weak residual expression of the 77-kDa PNPLA8 protein in Patient 12 (mild phenotype, p.Leu759Alafs*4) and in Patient 14 (non-neuronal phenotype, p.Val7*). In contrast, the homozygous missense variant p.Val520Asp from a previously reported patient with a severe phenotype gave protein levels similar to controls. The authors suggested that C-terminal truncating variants escape nonsense-mediated decay, leading to less severe disease.
quotes: LoF variants identified in non-severe cases (Patient 12, mild phenotype with p.Leu759Alafs*4; Patient 14, non-neuronal phenotype with p.Val7*) exhibited weak expression of the 77-kDa PNPLA8 protein, suggesting residual protein function (Supplementary Fig. 2C).

the missense variant identified in the previously reported patient (severe phenotype with homozygous p.Val520Asp) resulted in a similar protein expression level to the controls despite the severe phenotype
the C-terminal truncating variant is likely to avoid NMD and lead to less severe clinical manifestations

findings.statement: In 2 unrelated Iranian families from a non-neurological cohort, Nakamura et al. (2024) identified individuals homozygous for distinct N-terminal PNPLA8 frameshift variants that affect only the largest (88-kDa) isoform. One proband had optic atrophy and the other had nonsyndromic hearing loss. In the optic atrophy family, an affected sib was only heterozygous for the variant, so the authors considered these variants of undetermined significance.
quotes: we identified two additional individuals from two unrelated Iranian families with biallelic variants in PNPLA8 from another non-neurological cohort (Families 13 and 14; Supplementary Fig. 2A and B and Supplementary Table 1). A patient from one family showed optic atrophy, and the other patient showed non-syndromic hearing loss.

It is worth noting that in the family showing optic atrophy, there was an affected sibling of the proband, while he was heterozygous for the variant (Supplementary Fig. 2B). These findings indicate the undetermined significance of these N-terminal frameshift variants

findings.statement: In skin fibroblasts from Patient 1, Nakamura et al. (2024) found significantly lower maximal mitochondrial respiration than in healthy controls, although mitochondrial morphology was normal on electron microscopy. Cardiolipin and monolysocardiolipin appeared decreased in patient fibroblasts compared with controls but did not correlate with phenotypic severity.
quotes: Transmission electron microscopy analysis did not reveal altered mitochondrial morphology in the patient-derived skin fibroblasts (Supplementary Fig. 6B). However, live-cell assessment of mitochondrial OXPHOS activity using an extracellular flux analyser revealed that the maximal respiration level was significantly lower in the patient-derived skin fibroblasts than those from healthy controls

Although a significant correlation was not observed between CL/MLCL abundance and phenotypic severity, the abundance of CL and MLCL appeared to be decreased in patient-derived skin fibroblasts compared with control samples

findings.statement: Nakamura et al. (2024) made cerebral organoids from CRISPR/Cas9 PNPLA8-knockout human iPSCs and from iPSCs of Patient 1. These organoids had a smaller subventricular zone-like region, fewer PAX6+HOPX+ basal radial glial cells and fewer SATB2+ upper-layer neurons, while deep-layer neurons and basal intermediate progenitors were unchanged. Knockout neural progenitors had normal mitochondrial morphology and respiration but reduced lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), lysophosphatidylethanolamine and phosphatidic acid, and adding LPA partly restored the number of basal radial glia in patient organoids.
quotes: The number of PAX6+HOPX+ bRGCs in the SVZ was significantly reduced in PNPLA8 KO cerebral organoids compared with WT cerebral organoids (Fig. 4A and B).
The amounts of LPA, LPE and PA were decreased in PNPLA8 KO NPCs compared with WT NPCs, whereas there was no significant difference in that of other phospholipids and free fatty acids (Fig. 7E).
Treatment with LPA increased the number of bRGCs in Patient 1-derived cerebral organoids (Fig. 7F and G).

relevance_reason: Reports three new patients from two families with PNPLA8 variants and expands the phenotypic spectrum of PNPLA8-related mitochondriopathy, the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) reported 3 patients from 2 families with PNPLA8-related mitochondriopathy. Patient 1 (Family I) had the congenital form of the disease. Patients 2 and 3 (Family II) had progressive microcephaly, seizures starting in infancy, progressive cortical atrophy, loss of white matter, bilateral degeneration of the basal ganglia, and cystic encephalomalacia.
quotes: Patient 1 presented with the congenital form of the disease while Patients 2 and 3 showed progressive microcephaly, infantile onset seizures, progressive cortical atrophy, white matter loss, bilateral degeneration of basal ganglia, and cystic encephalomalacia.

findings.statement: In Patient 1 (Family I), who had the congenital form of PNPLA8-related mitochondriopathy, Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) used exome sequencing to identify a loss-of-function variant in the PNPLA8 gene, c.1231C>T (p.Arg411Ter).
quotes: exome sequencing identified a loss of function variant (c.1231C>T, p.Arg411Ter) in Family I

findings.statement: In Patients 2 and 3 (Family II), who had infantile-onset disease, Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) used exome sequencing to identify a missense variant in the PNPLA8 gene, c.1559T>A (p.Val520Asp).
quotes: a missense variant (c.1559T>A, p.Val520Asp) in Family II in PNPLA8

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) proposed infantile onset as a new, distinct phenotype of PNPLA8-related disease. They suggested that age at disease onset correlates strongly with where the variant lies, not with what type of variant it is. They described the PNPLA8-related conditions as a spectrum of overlapping features that line up with different ages of onset.
quotes: our results add the infantile onset as a new distinct phenotype of the disease and suggest that the site of the variant rather than its type is strongly correlated with the disease onset.
these conditions demonstrate some overlapping features representing a spectrum with clinical features always aligning with different age of onset.

findings.statement: Abdel-Hamid et al. (2024) noted that only 6 patients with biallelic PNPLA8 variants had been reported before. Reported phenotypes were a congenital form (congenital microcephaly, early-onset epileptic encephalopathy, and early death), a childhood neurodegeneration form with progressive microcephaly, and an adult-onset form with cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy.
quotes: Pathogenic variants in PNPLA8 have been described either with congenital onset displaying congenital microcephaly, early onset epileptic encephalopathy and early lethality or childhood neurodegeneration with progressive microcephaly.
a phenotype comprising adulthood onset cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy was also reported
only six patients with biallelic variants in PNPLA8 have been reported so far

relevance_reason: Reports 2 siblings with biallelic PNPLA8 loss-of-function variants, extending the PNPLA8-associated mitochondrial disease phenotype to a milder adolescent-onset ataxia/neuropathy.

findings.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) described 2 adult Lithuanian siblings (a brother and sister) who had slowly progressive cerebellar ataxia and sensorimotor axonal polyneuropathy with onset at age 14 years and preserved cognition. The brother, aged 49 at the time of the report, had lower-limb weakness and distal muscle atrophy, ataxia and gait disturbance, tetraparesis, absent lower-limb tendon reflexes, foot deformities, bilateral Babinski signs, dysmetria, and mild distal hypoesthesia. He became nonambulant at age 44 years. At age 45 he had mild dysarthria, horizontal nystagmus, and a normal Mini-Mental State Examination score, and brain MRI showed mild cerebellar atrophy. His sister had severe axial ataxia, appendicular dysmetria, distal muscle atrophy, areflexia, and bilateral Babinski signs at age 21. EMG showed no myopathic changes.
quotes: Both siblings presented with adolescence-onset ataxia, progressive sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and preserved cognition over time.
Sibling A became nonambulant at the age of 44 years. A neurologic examination at the age of 45 years showed mild dysarthria and horizontal nystagmus.
EMG revealed sparse abnormal spontaneous activity in the distal muscles of the lower limbs without myopathic changes.

findings.statement: In 2 siblings with adolescent-onset cerebellar ataxia and peripheral neuropathy, Burnyte et al. (2023) used whole-exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous frameshift variants in exon 11 of the PNPLA8 gene: a novel c.2269del (p.Thr757GlnfsTer10) and a previously reported c.2275_2276del (p.Leu759AlafsTer4). The c.2269del variant was not found in the ExAC, 1000 Genomes, or gnomAD databases. The c.2275_2276del variant was inherited from the mother. Paternal DNA was not available, but sequencing showed that the 2 variants were on different alleles (in trans), and Sanger sequencing confirmed both variants in the affected sister.
quotes: Exome sequencing revealed compound heterozygous loss-of-function variants c.2269del (p.(Thr757GlnfsTer10)) and c.2275_2276del (p.(Leu759AlafsTer4)) in PNPLA8.
This variant is not reported in the ExAC, 1000G, or gnomAD databases. The previously described c.2275_2276del variant was maternally inherited.
results of whole-exome sequencing and Sanger sequencing allowed us to ascertain that both changes were on different alleles (in trans) (Figure 1, B and C).

findings.statement: Burnyte et al. (2023) noted that c.2275_2276del had previously been reported in compound heterozygous state with another truncating variant in a patient with severe early-childhood neurodegeneration, whereas their patients had a milder phenotype. Because both truncating variants in their patients lie in the last coding exon of PNPLA8, the authors suggested that these transcripts may escape nonsense-mediated decay and possibly retain partial enzyme activity.
quotes: Of interest, c.2275_2276del has been reported in a compound heterozygous state with other variant leading to protein truncation and resulting in severe neurodegeneration manifesting in early childhood.

Both protein-truncating variants were identified in the last coding exon of PNPLA8 gene, suggesting that such transcripts may escape nonsense-mediated decay and possibly result in preserved partial enzyme activity and less severe clinical manifestation.

relevance_reason: Only the abstract is available. It describes a feasibility study of fast whole-genome sequencing of parents and child in 37 infants in intensive care (diagnostic yield 49%, rising to 57% after reanalysis). It does not mention mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis, any gene, or any variant, so there is nothing a curator could cite for this entry from the supplied text.
The paper reports a patient with a homozygous PNPLA8 missense variant and a severe phenotype. PNPLA8 is the gene behind mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis.

findings.statement: Masih et al. (2021) reported a patient with severe neurodegeneration that began before birth, progressed, and led to death in infancy.
quotes: The patient had prenatal-onset severe and progressive neurodegeneration with mortality in infancy.

findings.statement: In a patient with severe neurodegeneration that began before birth, Masih et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to find a novel homozygous missense variant, c.1874A>G, in the patatin domain of the PNPLA8 gene.
quotes: Using whole-exome sequencing, we identified a homozygous novel missense variation c.1874A>G in the patatin domain of PNPLA8.

relevance_reason: Reports two additional unrelated patients with biallelic loss-of-function PNPLA8 variants, with neurodegeneration and lactic acidosis, which expands the MMLA phenotype.

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) reported an Indian girl (patient 1) born to consanguineous parents. She had congenital microcephaly (head circumference -4 SD at birth) and multifocal clonic seizures starting on day 2 of life, along with spasticity of all four limbs. Brain MRI showed microcephaly with a simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum, a prominent cisterna magna with a hypoplastic cerebellum, and brainstem atrophy. MR spectroscopy showed an elevated lipid-lactate peak. TORCH testing was negative.
quotes: Weight was 2410 gm (−2 SD), length 48 cm (−1 SD) and head circumference 29 cm (−4 SD) at birth. On the second day of life, she had clonic movements in all four limbs and excessive cry.

She had multifocal clonic seizures and spasticity of all four limbs. Brain MRI showed microcephaly with simplified gyral pattern, hypoplasia of corpus callosum, prominent cisterna magna with hypoplastic cerebellum, brainstem atrophy (Figure 2A–C).
Magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) showed an elevated lipid-lactate peak.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated brain lactate level by MRS

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) reported a girl (patient 2) of Indian/Fijian origin born to nonconsanguineous parents. She developed normally until about 13 months of age and then regressed, with epilepsia partialis continua and focal seizures. She went on to have severe developmental stagnation and acquired microcephaly (-4.7 SD at age 15 years), and she was nonverbal and fed by gastrostomy tube. She also had hypotonia, proximal muscle weakness, absent reflexes, choreiform movements, dystonia and contractures. Progressive atrophy of the cerebrum, cerebellum and brainstem developed, MR spectroscopy showed a persistently elevated lipid-lactate peak, and she had hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with subaortic stenosis, abnormal visual evoked potentials, obstructive sleep apnea, elevated blood lactate and elevated GDF15.
quotes: By history, she had normal development until about 13 months of age. She was able to independently sit, stand, cruise, and babble. However, she then regressed concomitantly with several episodes of epilepsy partialis continua and difficult to control focal seizures.
Currently, at the age of 15 years, her head circumference was 49 cm (−4.7 SD). She developed involuntary choreiform movements, dystonia, proximal muscle weakness and absent muscle stretch reflexes.
Over the ensuing decade there was cortical volume loss in the cerebellum, brainstem, bilateral parietal and occipital lobes and corpus callosum thinning (Figure 2D–2L).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated brain lactate level by MRS

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) found that patient 2's muscle biopsy showed enlarged, irregularly shaped mitochondria with surrounding membrane whorls, disrupted cristae, electron-dense deposits, lipid droplets and glycogen pools. Activities of electron transport chain complexes I through IV were normal. GDF15 was elevated at 1293 pg/ml at age 14 years.
quotes: Muscle biopsy demonstrated enlarged and irregular shaped mitochondria on electron microscopy with surrounding membrane whorls. Electron dense deposits, lipid droplets, pools of glycogen and empty vacuoles, disrupted cristae. Electron transport chain enzymatic activities of complexes I – IV were within normal ranges.
at age 14 years, the patient had significantly elevated growth and differentiation factor 15 (1293 pg/ml; normal values <750 pg/ml)

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial respiratory chain

findings.statement: Using whole-exome sequencing, Shukla et al. (2018) identified a homozygous nonsense variant in PNPLA8, c.517G>T (p.Glu173Ter; NM_001256007.1), in patient 1, the daughter of consanguineous Indian parents. Sanger sequencing confirmed that both parents were heterozygous for the variant.
quotes: In patient, 1 we identified a homozygous nonsense variant in PNPLA8 [(c.517G>T, p.(Glu173Ter), NM_001256007.1] (Figure 1B).
Sanger sequencing of the variant, c.517G>T [p.(Glu173Ter), NM_001256007.1] in homozygous state in patient 1 and heterozygous state in the parents (D).

findings.statement: Using trio whole-exome sequencing, Shukla et al. (2018) identified compound heterozygous variants in PNPLA8 in patient 2. One was a frameshift variant, c.2275_2276delCT (p.Leu759AlafsTer4), and the other was a nonsense variant, c.419C>A (p.Ser140Ter). Sanger sequencing confirmed the variants, and each was inherited from a carrier parent.
quotes: Patient 2 was found to possess compound variants in PNPLA8, c.2275_2276delCT; p.(Leu759AlafsTer4) and c.419C>A; p.(Ser140Ter).
Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive pattern (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) found that the biallelic PNPLA8 variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
quotes: Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive pattern (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) noted that the 3 known patients with PNPLA8 loss-of-function variants had similar but variable clinical features. Because so few patients were known, they could not establish a genotype-phenotype correlation.
quotes: The clinical picture in the three patients with pathogenic variants in PNPLA8 is similar but variable.
Also, due to limited number of individuals, a genotype-phenotype correlation cannot be deduced at present.

findings.statement: Shukla et al. (2018) noted that all the PNPLA8 variants reported so far introduce premature stop codons and are likely to cause truncated protein or nonsense-mediated decay. They also observed that the abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes seen in patient 2 resembled findings in Pnpla8-null mice, and that the human phenotype resembled the progressive neurodegeneration seen in those mice.
quotes: The variants observed in PNPLA8, including the ones in our study are loss-of-function pathogenic variants, which introduce a premature stop codon (Figure 1E).

Histological findings in P2 of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes and inclusions were in concordance with the observations in the null-mice and the patient reported by Saunders et al..

relevance_reason: First report of PNPLA8-related mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis in a human patient, with compound heterozygous frameshift variants and functional protein studies.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) reported a 7-year-old girl (CMH193) with a suspected mitochondrial myopathy. She was asymptomatic in her first year and met developmental milestones, although toe-walking was noted. She had a positive Gowers sign at age 2 years and could no longer walk by age 3. Her course was progressive and included proximal muscle weakness, dysmetria, dysarthria, decline in fine motor skills, oral motor dystonia, hypotonia that progressed to spasticity, complex partial seizures with left temporal lobe spikes on EEG, a very lean body habitus without weight gain, and significant lactic acidosis requiring bicarbonate supplementation.
quotes: At age 2, she was noted to have a positive Gowers sign, and by the age of 3 years could no longer walk. Independent sitting was restricted to 10 minutes due to fatigue. Her fine motor skills declined and speech became dysarthric.

Hypotonicity progressed to spasticity of different opposing muscle groups. She recently developed complex partial seizures associated with recurrent left temporal lobe spikes on EEG, and slow wave discharges exacerbated by sleep.
In addition, she developed significant lactic acidosis, requiring bicarbonate supplementation.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) found that the patient had a persistently elevated anion gap from age 5 years. At age 7 she had elevated blood lactate (3.8-5.6 mmol/L) and pyruvate, with a lactate:pyruvate ratio that was not elevated, and a normal plasma acylcarnitine profile. CSF studies at age 6 showed 5-methyltetrahydrofolate deficiency. Creatine kinase and liver function tests were normal, mtDNA tRNA sequencing and mtDNA depletion studies were normal, and muscle SDH and COX activity and electron transport chain function were unaffected. The authors suggested this pattern indicated mitochondrial dysfunction rather than an electron transport chain defect.
quotes: At age 7, elevated lactic and pyruvic acid was demonstrated in blood on multiple occasions (lactic acid 3.8-5.6; n=0.7-2.1 mmol/L and pyruvic acid 0.18-0.32; n=0.08-0.16 mmol/L) with ratios of 17.5-21.1 (n=<20); plasma acylcarnitine profile was normal.

In the absence of an elevated lactate: pyruvate ratio, these results suggest mitochondrial dysfunction rather than an electron transport chain defect. Consistent with this concept, oxidative enzyme reactions (SDH and COX) showed normal activity in muscle (Supp. Figure S1), and electron transport chain function was not affected
Neurotransmitter studies in cerebrospinal fluid performed at the age of 6 showed deficiency of 5-methyltetrahydrofolate.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) reported that a quadriceps muscle biopsy taken at age 4 years showed variable fiber size with isolated small atrophic type 1 and type 2 fibers, and no ragged red fibers. Electron microscopy showed mitochondria with marked disarray of the cristae, globular dense osmiophilic inclusions, and subsarcolemmal aggregates of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes, suggestive of degenerating mitochondria. Secondary lysosomes containing residual bodies were increased. Brain MRI at 33 months showed subtle bilateral increased signal in the medial globus pallidus that was no longer seen 2 years later.
quotes: Specifically, mitochondria from CMH193 exhibit marked disarray of cristae and globular dense osmiophilic inclusions by EM analysis. In addition, subsarcolemmal aggregates of abnormal mitochondria with concentric lamellar membranes and dense round or oval, strongly osmiophilic inclusions were observed, suggestive of degenerating mitochondria
In addition, variable fiber size was found with isolated small atrophic fibers of all subtypes observed, but with no ragged red fibers (Fig. 1a).

Initial MRI brain scan at 33 months of age showed subtle increased signal intensity involving the medial globus pallidus bilaterally which was no longer visualized two years later at the second study, suggesting maturation of myelination.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Increased variability in muscle fiber diameter
Subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormally shaped mitochondria

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) performed trio exome sequencing and found that the patient was compound heterozygous for 2 frameshift variants in the PNPLA8 gene: c.334_337delAATT (p.Asn112HisfsX29) and c.1975_1976delAG (p.Leu659AlafsX4). Both variants were confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Each was inherited from a carrier parent, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, and 2 healthy sibs carried neither variant. Neither variant was present in the Exome Sequencing Project database or in an internal database of 1,913 samples.
quotes: the patient was compound heterozygous for two frameshift variants, c.334_337delAATT (p.Asn112HisfsX29) and c.1975_1976delAG (p.Leu659AlafsX4) in PNPLA8

Segregation analysis confirmed that the variants were inherited from carrier parents, consistent with an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. In addition, genotyping of two healthy siblings revealed they were negative for both variants.
Both PNPLA8 variants were absent from the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project (EVS; http://evs.gs.washington.edu/EVS/) and an internal variant database of 1913 samples.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) performed Western blot analysis on the patient's muscle and found a marked decrease in the 88-, 63-, and 52-kD PNPLA8 (iPLA2-gamma) protein bands compared with 3 control muscles. A 110-kD band present in controls was also absent; mass spectrometry identified this band as HSPA4, which the authors concluded had reacted nonspecifically with the antibody.
quotes: Western blot showing dramatic decrease of the 88, 63, and 52kD PNPLA8 protein (NP_001242940.1) in the muscle from CMH193, compared to muscle from three control samples with known non-mitochondrial diagnoses.
The results demonstrated the 110 kD band to be heat shock protein family member 4 (HSPA4) (Supp. Table S2).
Collectively, these results indicate that the “immunoreactivity” of the 110 kDa protein detected by Western blotting was due to a non-specific interaction of HSPA4 with the antibody.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) noted that the patient's phenotype and mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities closely resembled those of Pnpla8-null mice. These mice have mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired learning, decreased exercise endurance, a thin body habitus, and cold intolerance, as well as dysmorphic mitochondria in the myocardium and cerebellum. The authors suggested that this resemblance supported a causal link between the PNPLA8 variants and the patient's disease.
quotes: The Pnpla8 -/- mouse has mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired learning, decreased exercise endurance, enhanced insulin sensitivity, a thin body habitus (from energy dissipation by mitochondrial uncoupling), and cold intolerance.

In summary, a causal link between the proband's phenotype and PNPLA8 variantsis supported by the parallel alterations in neuromuscular dysfunction, cognitive deficits and the striking similarities in dysmorphic and degenerating mitochondria present in the Pnpla8 -/- mouse.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) suggested that, as in PLA2G6-related disease, PNPLA8-related disease may result primarily from altered mitochondrial inner membrane homeostasis, with effects on electron transport and ATP synthesis being secondary.
quotes: This may also be the case with PNPLA8-related disease, where proteins involved in electron transport and ATP synthesis located in the inner membranes would be secondarily affected by altered membrane homeostasis but not the primary pathogenic mechanism.

findings.statement: Saunders et al. (2015) reported that the patient's symptoms initially improved with a multivitamin containing iron, carbidopa-levodopa, and leucovorin. CoQ10 supplementation increased her appetite but did not lead to weight gain.
quotes: Treatment with a multivitamin containing iron, Carbidopa-Levodopa and leucovorin initially improved symptoms. Supplementation with CoQ10 increased appetite without subsequent weight gain, and persistence of a very lean body habitus.

relevance_reason: The paper describes a knockout mouse for iPLA2-gamma, the gene product linked to this disorder. The mice had mitochondrial degeneration and altered cardiolipin, which makes the paper relevant as an animal model. It reports no human patients.

findings.statement: Mancuso et al. (2009) found that iPLA2-gamma-null mice (iPLA2-gamma -/-) had major changes in hippocampal phospholipid metabolism and mitochondrial phospholipid homeostasis. Shotgun lipidomics showed a markedly raised hippocampal cardiolipin content, with the molecular species shifted toward shorter chains. The mice also had altered choline and ethanolamine glycerophospholipids, including less plasmenylethanolamine, along with more oxidized phosphatidylethanolamine species and more ceramides.
quotes: Shotgun lipidomics demonstrated multiple alterations in hippocampal lipid metabolism in iPLA(2)gamma(-/-) mice including: 1) a markedly elevated hippocampal cardiolipin content with an altered molecular species composition characterized by a shift to shorter chain length molecular species;

2) alterations in both choline and ethanolamine glycerophospholipids, including a decreased plasmenylethanolamine content; 3) increased oxidized phosphatidylethanolamine molecular species; and 4) an increased content of ceramides.

findings.statement: In iPLA2-gamma-null mice, Mancuso et al. (2009) saw enlarged, heteromorphic lamellar structures undergoing degeneration on electron microscopy, together with ubiquitin-positive spheroid inclusion bodies. Purification and proteomics identified these structures as degenerating mitochondria. The mice showed autophagy and cognitive dysfunction. The authors concluded that iPLA2-gamma has an obligatory role in neuronal mitochondrial lipid metabolism and membrane structure, and that its loss of function causes a mitochondrial neurodegenerative disorder.
quotes: Electron microscopic examination demonstrated the presence of enlarged heteromorphic lamellar structures undergoing degeneration accompanied by the presence of ubiquitin positive spheroid inclusion bodies.
Purification of these enlarged heteromorphic lamellar structures by buoyant density centrifugation and subsequent SDS-PAGE and proteomics identified them as degenerating mitochondria.
demonstrating that iPLA(2)gamma loss of function results in a mitochondrial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by degenerating mitochondria, autophagy, and cognitive dysfunction.

relevance_reason: Case report of mitochondrial myopathy with lactic acidosis, cardiomyopathy and lipid accumulation, with response to prednisone and thiamine.

findings.statement: Mastaglia et al. (1980) described a 23-year-old man with mitochondrial myopathy who had a high-output circulatory state and cardiomyopathy that caused cardiac insufficiency 22 years before the skeletal myopathy appeared. Venous lactate levels were elevated, and at one stage of the illness he developed severe lactic acidosis.
quotes: a 23-year-old male with a mitochondrial myopathy who had a high-output circulatory state and cardiomyopathy which resulted in cardiac insufficiency 22 years before presentation of the skeletal myopathy
Venous lactate levels were elevated and severe lactic acidosis developed at one stage of the illness.

findings.statement: In the patient reported by Mastaglia et al. (1980), electron microscopy of muscle showed various mitochondrial abnormalities and an accumulation of neutral lipids. The lipid accumulation was confirmed by histochemistry and thin-layer chromatography.
quotes: Electron microscopy of muscle tissue showed various mitochondrial abnormalities and accumulation of neutral lipids which was confirmed histochemically and by thin-layer chromatography.

findings.statement: Mastaglia et al. (1980) observed a marked improvement in their patient's myopathy after he started prednisone and thiamine. The improvement continued after both drugs were withdrawn.
quotes: Marked improvement in the myopathy occurred after commencement of prednisone and thiamine and was maintained following withdrawal of these drugs.

findings.statement: Mastaglia et al. (1980) did not define the metabolic defect in their patient. They postulated an abnormality involving the Krebs cycle that resulted in overproduction of lactate and lipid accumulation in muscle.
quotes: The metabolic defect in this case has not been defined, but an abnormality in the Kreb's over-production of lactate and lipid accumulation in muscle is postulated.

relevance_reason: The title describes a metabolic myopathy with chronic lactic acidemia, which matches the subject of this entry. Only the title was available, so details are limited.

findings.statement: Hackett et al. (1973) described a metabolic myopathy associated with chronic lactic acidemia, growth failure, and nerve deafness.
quotes: A metabolic myopathy associated with chronic lactic acidemia, growth failure, and nerve deafness.
